sentences.text: Ju Dg M E Nt

The petitioners have filed this petition U/s 166 of the Motor vehicles Act claiming compensation for the death of Shivakumar D.S. in a motor vehicle accident Shylaja vs B.M.T.C on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19217493/
1 that occurred on 3.3.2022.
2. The case of the petitioners, in brief, is as follows:

On 3.3.2022 at about 10.50 p.m. the deceased was proceeding on the motor cycle bearing No. KA-02-JH- 1517 from Prasanna junction to M.C. circle and when he reached near Cholurpalya junction, Magadi road, the driver of BMTC bus bearing No. KA-57-F-3319, which was going in front of the deceased vehicle was driving t he  3 SCCH-17 MVC No. 923-2023 said bus in a rash and negligent manner and suddenly applied the break and stopped the bus in the center of the road.
Due to the impact the deceased dashed to the back side of the BMTC bus and fell down and sustained fracture injuries and head injury.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Spine Care Hospital, but he succumbed to the said injuries.
The petitioners have spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards funeral and other incidental expenses.

At the time of accident, the deceased was working as Store Manager at O Aurora Ventures and earning Rs.40,000/- p.m. and he was contributing the same to his family maintenance, but due to untimely death of deceased the petitioners have suffered mentally and physically.
The petitioners No.1 is the mother and petitioner No.2 is the sister of the deceased,
have lost love and affection and care taker.

The  4 SCCH-17 MVC No. 923-2023 Shylaja vs B.M.T.C on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19217493/
2 respondent is the owner cum insurer of the BMTC bus is liable to pay compensation compensation to the petitioners.

Hence the petitioners prays to award compensation of Rs.40,00,000/-
 3.

After service of notice the respondent appeared and filed written statement by contending that the accident was occurred due to negligent riding of the motor cycle by the deceased himself and there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the BMTC bus bearing No. KA- 57-F-3319 and the deceased was not having valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased.
The compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, the respondent prays to dismiss the petition against it.

On the basis of the rival contentions, the following issues were framed by this court:
 ISSUES  1) Whether the petitioners proves that  deceased Shivakumar D.S. died in the  motor vehicle accident that occurred on  3.3.2022 at about 10.50 p.m. near  Cholurpalya junction, Magadi road,
 Bengaluru due to the rash and negligence  driving of the BMTC bus bearing No. KA-  57-F-3319 by its driver?

Shylaja vs B.M.T.C on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19217493/
3  2.
Whether the petitioners prove that they are  the legal heirs and dependents of  deceased?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for  compensation?
If so, what amount and  from whom?
4. What order or award?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, petitioner No.1 is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.8.
The respondent in spite of sufficient opportunity has not chosen to lead evidence.
6 SCCH-17 MVC No. 923-2023
6. I have heard the arguments of learned counsel for both the parties and perused the material available on record.
7. My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1: In the negative,
 Issue No.2:

In the affirmative,
 Issue No.3:

In the negative,
 Issue No.4: As per final orders  for the following.-
 REASONS  ISSUE NO.1:
 8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner No.1 has filed er affidavit in lieu of chief examination, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of her claim, she has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, IMV report, notice issued to owner of the vehicle and reply issued by him, PM  7 SCCH-17 MVC No. 923-2023 Shylaja vs B.M.T.C on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19217493/
4 report and charge sheet, which are marked as Ex.P1 to 6 and8.
 9.
The PW.1 who is the mother of the deceased examined herself as PW.1 by alleging the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the BMTC bus bearing no. KA-57-F-3319.

It is the case of the petitioners that the driver of bus bearing No. KA-57-F-3319 has driven the said bus in a high speed with rash and negligent manner without observing the traffic signals suddenly applied the break and stopped the bus in the centre of the road, due to which, the deceased who is coming in the back side of the BMTC bus has got dashed against the back side of the bus and got head injuries and died due to the fatal injuries sustained by him.
10. To prove the said allegations, the PW.1 who is the mother of the deceased examined hereself as PW.1  8 SCCH-17 MVC No. 923-2023 and produced Ex.P1 to 8 documents.
The Pw.1 admitted in the cross-examination that she is not an eye witness and has no personal knowledge about the accident and she is deposing the evidence on the basis of the documents.
Hence, the evidence of the PW.1 has to be read with the documents produced by her.

Out of the Ex.P1 to 8, except the Ex.P8 copies of Aadhaar card all Shylaja vs B.M.T.C on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19217493/
5 other documents are police documents of Crime No.16- 2022 on the file of Magadi Road Traffic police station.

11. The Ex.P2 first information is lodged by the conductor of bus bearing No. KA-57-F-3319 wherein he alleged that while they were proceeding near Magadi Road, Prasanna junction, the rider of the bike bearing No.
KA-02-JH-5147 by driving his bike in a rash and negligent manner has dashed against the back side of their bus and fell down and thereby got fatal injuries to  9 SCCH-17 MVC No. 923-2023 the head and other parts of the body.
No doubt that soon after the accident, the deceased has severely injured.

The information is given by the conductor of bus bearing No.
KA-57-F-3319 against whom the present petition is filed by seeking compensation.
On the basis of Ex.P2, Ex.P1 FIR is registered.
Thereafter, the IO has conducted the spot mahazar as per Ex.P3.
The Ex.P3 also appended with rough sketch.
On perusal of the contents of Ex.P3 mahazar and rough sketch the alleged accident spot is in the left side of the road and the deceased has dashed against the back side of the BMTC bus.
The contents of Ex.P.3 rough sketch and mahazar falsifies the contention of petitioners about sudden stopping of the bus by its driver in the middle of the road.
12. The Ex.P3 mahazar also speaks about the damages found on both the vehicles.

The Ex.P4 is IMV Shylaja vs B.M.T.C on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19217493/
6  10 SCCH-17 MVC No. 923-2023 report wherein the damages found on both the vehicles is mentioned.
As per Ex.P4 the front portion of the bike of the deceased is got damaged and the bus has got lighter damage in its rear left side.
Thereby once again it falsifies the contention of the petitioners regarding the rash and negligent driving by the driver of BMTC bus and stopping of the bus in the middle of the road.

13. It is very important to note that the petitioners except the police documents which are marked at Ex.P6 & 8, has not relied on any other documents to prove their case and also to prove the negligence on the part of driver of BMTC bus.
The respondent contended that the deceased was not having valid driving licence.
To over come the said contention, the Pw.1 has not produced the driving licence of the deceased.

No eye witness are examined before this court and no efforts are made by the  11 SCCH-17 MVC No. 923-2023 petitioners to examine the IO to bring out the lacunas in his investigations to hold the negligence of the driver of BMTC bus.
The police documents and head of the charge sheet depicts the negligence by the deceased.
No independent evidence is adduced to disbelieve the contents of police documents.

Except the police Shylaja vs B.M.T.C on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19217493/
7 documents no other evidence is available to probabalise the case of the petitioners.

14. The petition is filed under Sec. 166 of IMV Act,
wherein proving of the negligence by the driver of offending vehicle is sine-qua-non (a necessary condition without which something is not possible ) to grant the compensation.
In this case, the petitioners failed to establish the prima facie point of negligence on the basis of pre-ponderance of probabilities.
No evidence is available to accept the case of the petitioners.

Hence,
 12 SCCH-17 MVC No. 923-2023 without any hesitation, this tribunal holds this issue in negative.
ISSUE NO.2  15.
As contended in the petition the petitioner No.1 is the mother of the deceased and petitioner No.2 is the sister of the deceased.
In the cause title itself the petitioner No.2 is shown as married.
The respondent do not specifically deny the relationship of petitioners with deceased.
The petitioners to prove their relationship with deceased, have produced the notarized copies of Aaadhar cards of petitioners which are marked under Ex.P.7.
During the course of recording the evidence the notarized copies of Aadhar cards are compared with the original documents and found correct.
As per these documents the petitioners are the mother and sister of deceased.

Shylaja vs B.M.T.C on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19217493/
8
The respondents do not dispute the relationship of the  13 SCCH-17 MVC No. 923-2023 petitioners with deceased.
The respondent do not dispute the Aadhaar cards produced by the petitioners.
The respondent have not adduced any evidence to disprove the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.
Accordingly, issue No. 2 answered in the affirmative.
ISSUE NO.3
16. In the present issue three sub points are involved.
One is whether the petitioners are entitle for the compensation.
Secondly, if they are entitle, what amount has to be awarded and lastly who is liable to pay the compensation.
To consider later two points, the petitioners first has to establish that they are entitle for the compensation.

17. As discussed above, the issue No.1 is already answered in the negative, wherein the petitioners failed to  14 SCCH-17 MVC No. 923-2023 prove the negligence by the driver of bus bearing No. KA- 57-F-3319.
18. By considering all the above points, in the present case on hand, the alleged accident is not due to the mechanical defect as per Ex.P4- IMV report.

The Shylaja vs B.M.T.C on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19217493/
9
deceased is charge sheeted and no other grounds are made out by the petitioners to show that the accident is caused by the negligence of the other party and not due to the negligence of deceased.
The awarding of compensation is governed under Sec. 147 of IMV Act.
The present petition is also filed under Sec. 166 of IMV Act.

Admittedly the present petition is filed under Sec.
166 of IMV Act, wherein the negligence has to be proved.
Only upon proving of the negligence, the injured or the dependents of the deceased are entitle for the compensation.
When the petition is filed under Sec. 163- 15 SCCH-17 MVC No. 923-2023 A of IMV Act, then considering the part of negligence is not relevant.
But while considering the petition under Sec. 166 of IMV Act, the concept of negligence places very important role.
19. The liability under Sec. 147 the insurance company is to the extent of indemnification of the insured against the third person.
In this case, the deceased himself is the sole responsible person for the said accident.
Such being the case, when a person himself is negligible for the accident is not entitled for the compensation.

Hence, the petitioners being the legal heirs of the deceased are not entitle for the compensation under Sec. 166 of IMV Act.
 20.

When it is considered that the petitioners are Shylaja vs B.M.T.C on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19217493/
10 not entitle for the compensation, the question of  16 SCCH-17 MVC No. 923-2023 considering the amount and liability will not arise.

ISSUE NO.4:-
 21.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby dismissed.
No order as to costs.
Draw the award accordingly.
